decisions.evidence: R1 maker: “Save a bookmark: enter an address, it's stored and listed.” R1 client requested additions but did not challenge URL-based saving.
decisions.note: The baseline save behavior conforms at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented only “Auto-fetches page titles.” R1 client corrected this to collect “title, description, site icon, and preview image—not only its title.”
decisions.note: The initial metadata behavior was incomplete; the client supplied the reference-conforming metadata set at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker mentioned auto-derived titles and generic correction of details. R1 client required that title and description be adjustable “before saving and later.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing before-and-after edit timing and fields.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker only said “Edit & delete: correct details.” R1 client explicitly mentioned later title/description adjustment and Markdown notes, but the transcript does not expose whether the presented spec allowed editing every required field: URL, title, description, tags, and note.
decisions.note: The presentation is too abbreviated to establish either conformity or divergence for the complete editable-field set.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: “delete with a confirmation step.” R1 client did not contest deletion.
decisions.note: Permanent deletion was present at the initial specification gate; confirmation is an additional UI safeguard.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker's stated baseline contained no duplicate-save behavior. R1 client: “Saving the same address again should not create a duplicate. It should take me to the existing bookmark so I can edit it.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing duplicate-convergence requirement.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker only promised to “list everything.” R1 client required a readability-focused list showing “title, description, tags, and site icon.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing per-item list contents and presentation goal.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: “open a bookmark in a new tab.” R1 client did not challenge this behavior.
decisions.note: Opening the selected bookmark at its original URL is conforming; new-tab navigation is an equivalent UI choice.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: “Organize by flexible tags (a bookmark can have several).” R1 client confirmed a preference for flexible tags rather than folders.
decisions.note: Multiple tags per bookmark conformed at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented flexible tagging without suggestions; the revised-spec presentation in R7 still lacked this behavior. R7 client: “When I enter tags, suggest existing tags so I can reuse them consistently.”
decisions.note: The omission persisted through the revised-spec gate and was then corrected. It is counted once, linked to its eventual disposition.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: “apply tags, filter to one tag, clear the filter.” R1 client did not challenge single-tag filtering.
decisions.note: The tag-filter behavior conformed at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker limited search to “title/address.” R1 client corrected it to cover “title, description, note, and address.”
decisions.note: The initial full-text field set was incomplete.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker did not state case handling. R1 client required search to work “without caring about capitalization.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing case-insensitive-search rule.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented only basic title/address search. R1 client requested richer searching with “#tag.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing tag-search syntax.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented only basic search. R1 client requested “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.”
decisions.note: The client added Boolean operators and grouped expressions at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: The R1/R7 presented search scope omitted the quoted-operator rule. R7 client specified that AND/OR/NOT act as operators normally but as ordinary exact text “when placed in quotes.”
decisions.note: The distinct quoted-operator edge case was caught at the revised-spec gate and is not double-counted as an earlier pending omission.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented basic title/address search. R1 client requested “quoted exact phrases.”
decisions.note: The client added exact-phrase search.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker's listed journeys had no read-later state. R1 client: “I need a ‘read later’ state.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing unread flag behavior.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker omitted an unread perspective. R1 client requested “a separate unread view.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing unread-only view.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker omitted read-state transitions. R1 client requested “a way to mark items read.”
decisions.note: The client added removal from the unread queue through marking read.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker's baseline had no multi-selection or bulk actions. R1 client requested selecting bookmarks for bulk tag, read-status, archive, and delete changes.
decisions.note: The complete selected-item bulk-action capability was added by the client.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker omitted whole-result-set actions. R1 client: “Applying an action to all matching results should respect the current search or filter.”
decisions.note: The client added the filter-scoped whole-collection rule.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker did not present sorting. R1 client: “Please include sorting.”
decisions.note: The missing sort capability was added at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker's baseline had no note entity or note journey. R1 client requested “a personal note, including formatted Markdown.”
decisions.note: The client added Markdown note authoring/rendering.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker's baseline omitted preserved copies. R1 client requested a local copy and specified “using the original PDF when the link is a PDF.”
decisions.note: The client added both local snapshot preservation and the PDF rule.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker omitted Internet Archive support. R1 client asked to “offer an Internet Archive copy as well.”
decisions.note: The missing Internet Archive snapshot capability was added.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker's baseline did not include archiving. R1 client required archived items to “stay out of the normal list and ordinary searches.”
decisions.note: The client added archive behavior and its default-list/search exclusion rule.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented deletion but no distinct archive state. R1 client: “Archiving should be reversible and separate from deleting.”
decisions.note: The client added the reversible-archive versus permanent-delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker omitted an archive perspective. R1 client required archived items to “have their own view.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing archived-only list.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker omitted reusable filters. R1 client requested saved filters combining “a search with included and excluded tags.”
decisions.note: The client added bundles with all required filter components.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker omitted import. R1 client requested browser bookmark HTML import preserving “titles, tags, and saved dates.”
decisions.note: The client added Netscape-format import and preservation requirements.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker omitted export. R1 client requested export in “the common browser bookmark HTML format.”
decisions.note: The client added Netscape-format export.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker omitted user display settings. R1 client requested “default sorting, how many items are shown, and text size.”
decisions.note: The client added the required display preferences.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker offered duplicate normalization policies; R2 client selected light normalization while keeping distinct paths and meaningful queries separate.
decisions.note: The selected normalization still converges repeated equivalent URLs to the existing bookmark. Treatment of near-identical URLs beyond the reference rule is an orthogonal edge-policy choice.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker offered default read-state choices. R3 client selected: “new bookmarks should start as read” and enter unread only when deliberately marked read later.
decisions.note: The selected opt-in read-later workflow conforms; the reference does not require a particular default state.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker offered duplicate-import policies. R4 client selected non-destructive merging that unions tags, fills empty fields, and keeps the earliest saved date.
decisions.note: The selected duplicate-import policy preserves required imported data; collision precedence beyond that is not fixed by the reference.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker offered snapshot-fidelity choices. R5 client selected a “full-page copy” in one file and the original PDF for PDF links.
decisions.note: The selected snapshot representation conforms; exact visual fidelity is not otherwise fixed by the reference.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker offered a folder-mapping option under which “a multi-tag bookmark must be duplicated across folders.” R6 client selected the common TAGS attribute “so multiple tags survive import and export without creating duplicate bookmarks.”
decisions.note: The alternatives differed in multi-tag and duplicate-free fulfillment; the client selected the reference-conforming representation.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker offered trimming the large v1, explicitly suggesting deferral of “preserved copies or saved filters.” R7 client responded: “I’m happy with the scope and don’t want to trim it.”
decisions.note: At the revised-spec gate, the client selected the full reference-conforming scope over offered omissions.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker documented sort options as “saved-date / title / recently-updated.” R7 client did not contest them.
decisions.note: These options satisfy sorting by a chosen key.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker stated that when no archive copy exists, the app “offers to request a snapshot.” R7 client did not contest this behavior.
decisions.note: Offering to create an Internet Archive snapshot conforms.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker said “oversize local copies [are] marked unavailable”; R9 made this concrete as “Size cap 25 MB → oversize copies marked unavailable.” R7 client said the scope was satisfactory except for two unrelated details, and R9 client gave general plan approval without identifying the missing-copy departure.
decisions.note: The cap leaves qualifying oversized pages without the required preserved local copy. Neither response explicitly surfaced or accepted that difference.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker revised the spec so typing a tag suggests matching existing tags and selecting one reuses it. R8 client approved.
decisions.note: The corrected tag-autocomplete decision conforms at the final specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker revised search so AND/OR/NOT are operators unquoted and literal text inside quotes. R8 client approved.
decisions.note: The corrected quoted-operator rule conforms at the final specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker planned SQLite FTS5 plus a custom Boolean parser/AST to support quoted literals and #tag semantics. R9 client said the plan preserved the agreed behavior.
decisions.note: The search implementation is functionally equivalent to the reference requirements.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker planned “MHTML captured via Playwright + Chromium” with original PDF storage. R9 client approved the plan.
decisions.note: MHTML is a single-file local HTML archive and is functionally conforming; the separate size-cap departure is classified independently.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker planned Markdown rendering with markdown-it and DOMPurify sanitization. R9 client approved.
decisions.note: Sanitized Markdown rendering conforms.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker stated metadata, capture, and Wayback operations would be attempted but degrade gracefully when outbound service access is unavailable. R9 client explicitly found “graceful handling of unavailable external services” acceptable.
decisions.note: Transient external-service failure handling does not remove the supported capabilities and is not a reference divergence.

decisions.evidence: R10 maker offered adjusting scope, “e.g., defer P4 stories,” alongside full implementation. R10 client instructed implementation of “the full scope” and stated that the US1+US2 checkpoint “should not be treated as the completed first release.”
decisions.note: At the task gate, the client selected the complete reference-conforming release over an offered reduced/deferred scope.

decisions.evidence: R10 maker described US1+US2 as a reviewable MVP checkpoint before implementation continued. R10 client accepted reviewing that checkpoint while requiring the full release afterward.
decisions.note: A temporary review checkpoint does not itself remove later requirements and was conforming.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker presented implemented URL saving with editable metadata and duplicate-free light normalization. R11 client said the implemented behavior matched the approval and accepted the application.
decisions.note: The presented implementation of the save and duplicate workflow conforms.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker presented rich search with #tag, phrases, Boolean operators, parentheses, and quoted operators as literals, backed by passing grammar tests. R11 client accepted the application.
decisions.note: The implementation-review search decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker presented tags with suggestions, read-later, archive, sort, bulk actions, and “apply to all matching.” R11 client accepted the behavior.
decisions.note: The presented organization, status, filtering, and bulk-action implementation conforms.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker presented Markdown notes, saved filters, MHTML/PDF copies, Internet Archive support, Netscape HTML import/export with TAGS, and display preferences. R11 client accepted the application.
decisions.note: Apart from the separately classified oversized-copy cap, the presented extended-feature implementation conforms.
